correctness.rationale: Symmetrizing a finite pseudometric preserves both sums. Triangle constraints in the four-orbit family are sufficient, and strict monotonicity of within-part contributions reduces to a single fractional-linear objective. Its derivative sign equals sign(4a-b-3) on [0,1], and it strictly decreases on [1,2]. Feasible shortest-path and collapsed-star witnesses attain the two exact branches. A cut identity forbids the graph metric on K_{a,a} from being L1 for a>=3; the finite cut cone is closed, normalized feasible metrics compact, so any purported L1 equality would symmetrize to the forbidden unique optimizer. The star metric is explicitly L1 and sharp above the threshold. Reproduced finite exact diagnostics: 4550 orbit points, 4408 cut vectors, 1482 L1 cut identities.
